::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--operations}
Operations Manual
:::

**Status:** Operational framework.
**Owner:** BNR Lead and BNR Developer.

## Purpose

Maintain enough evidence and current guidance for another authorised operator to understand, reproduce and safely continue routine work.

## Records to maintain


| Stage         | Record                                                              | Where it is kept and why                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Before REDCap** | Registry definitions and abstraction instructions                   | This manual is the official reference for which cases to include, what information to collect and how to record it.                                                                                                  |
| **Before REDCap** | Source-record references and evidence used to support an entry      | The original clinical or registry source system remains the authoritative source. REDCap should retain only the necessary reference or summary, not duplicate identifiable source material.                          |
| **Before REDCap** | Cases needing clinical review or clarification                      | Record the outstanding issue and final decision with the relevant registry record, so that decisions requiring clinical judgement can be understood later.                                                           |
| **REDCap**        | Live registry records, corrections and material correction reasons  | REDCap holds the current record. Its audit trail preserves what changed and when; record the reason for a material correction with the affected record where needed.                                                 |
| **REDCap**        | Data-entry rules and live project configuration                     | This manual explains the rules; REDCap holds the live forms, fields, validation and user-facing configuration. Keep a current configuration export with the private handover records when a material change is made. |
| **REDCap**        | Authorised users and their access roles                             | REDCap User Rights is the live record of access. The private local configuration sheet records the responsible contacts and access-recovery information. Review both when staff responsibilities change.             |
| **REDCap**        | Outstanding data-quality queries                                    | Keep unresolved queries with the affected REDCap record, and close them when resolved. Do not maintain a duplicate process / spreadsheet unless BNR later adopts one for a defined purpose.                                    |
| **After REDCap**  | Protected extracts, processing logs, staging files and review files | The private BNR workspace holds these restricted working files. They must not be placed in the public repository.                                                                                                    |
| **After REDCap**  | Release version, package contents and approval evidence             | The approved data package contains its dataset period and version, package ID, manifest and `approval.yml`. Together these show exactly what was approved for release and by whom.                                        |
| **After REDCap**  | Approved public-release packages                                    | The approved copy in authoritative public storage outside Git is the official release and must not be edited by hand.                                                                                                |
|**After REDCap**  | Website copy and supporting documentation                           | Public-safe Info-Hub repository paths hold the website copy. This is a mirror that can be recreated from the approved release.                                                                                       |
| **After REDCap**  | History of changes to code and documentation                        | The Git repository is the official record of changes to code and documentation, using its commit history.                                                                                                            |
| **All stages** | Private access and recovery arrangements | Keep the responsible roles, restricted file locations and recovery contacts in the appropriate institutional access records. Do not store passwords or access tokens in Git or in the manual. |
| **All stages**  | Significant changes made after handover                             | The concise change history records only changes that materially affect methods, approval, publication, disclosure control, required software or staff responsibilities.                                              |
                             |

## Routine maintenance

- Keep role assignments and the private configuration sheet up to date.
- Check that a second authorised person can find and run each routine workflow.
- Keep the commands and instructions in the Technical Manual in step with the current files and dialogs.
- Remove out-of-date navigation rather than leaving empty public pages.
- Check software requirements, such as Python and Git, before upgrading Stata, Quarto, Python or any extensions.

## Handover checklist

The person handing over and the person taking over should check together that:

- The new operator has been given the access they need through the usual BNR or institutional process.
- The right people hold the local file locations and access details.
- Everyone knows which release is the latest complete version, and what work is still under way.
- Any unresolved questions, failed runs and approvals still needed are clearly listed.
- The usual workflow can be run safely, either as a test or during the current reporting cycle.
- Everyone understands who is responsible for backup and recovery.
- The current repository branch and Git status are clear.
- Access for people who no longer need it has been removed.

## Recording important changes after handover

Keep a short record of any change that affects:

- How a measure is defined.
- How work is approved or published.
- The structure of public outputs.
- Confidentiality protection.
- Software that the system needs.
- Who is responsible for a task.

Small routine changes only need a clear record in Git.

## Annual review and review after staff changes

At least once a year—and whenever a key member of staff leaves or a core system changes—review:

- This manual and the Technical Manual.
- Who is responsible for each role.
- The private configuration sheet.
- Required software and other dependencies.
- Access rights.
- Backup and recovery arrangements.
